impl.summary: Picked up the pushed branch (6 commits on f7c6d8e, only this package's own work) and merged claude/fuobe-parity-4 in twice, because the base moved during the session (4e51ffb, then bcfeb63). Conflicts were resolved keeping both sides in 14 files, including generations.ts (main's account checks plus the restore graph's LoRAs), gen-cloud-models.py (main's new Evolution plus the Restore model), the comfy README, library spec, install script, manifest and settings-form. The generated cloud-model and LoRA-library files match their generators. Then I finished the package. Its three routes are plain route exports again, following the public sign-up rules. Gated LoRAs behave as they did before the branch, except Restore's own adapter. The Hugging Face download token is now its own setting. The flaky test is fixed. Upscale's 'Restore archive footage first' now restores then upscales in one run. The GPU pre-flight board has a row for the tool, and the requirement index lists its graph. The e2e and the browser checks were run.
built: Routes: /api/restore and /api/restore/prompt are plain POST exports. Guests and accounts get 403 own-gpu-tool from the proxy (with or without a GPU) because the tool plans with the studio's own AI helpers and chains its steps on the server. So no account run reads a file here, and tenant/account-inputs don't come into it. An account's single fuobe-restore run through POST /api/generations already goes through main's checks (accountRun, checkAccountLoras sees the graph's gated LoRA). /api/restore/estimate is in ESTIMATES and runs through priceAs: a visitor is priced on its own GPU, never as a demo.
The page shows SelfHostNote, 'Self-hosted only' pricing and disabled inputs to visitors, the way Evolution does.

The prompt writer uses src/server/llm (probeLocal, localWhat, localLabel). It answers with by 'local' instead of 'ollama', and the UI says 'a local model' and 'Settings → AI helper'. Frames are capped at 900 KB each (4 at most), so the body stays under the proxy's 4 MB.

Hugging Face download token: main already had huggingfaceToken (Assist's Hugging Face Inference Providers key) on the same stored key, which made a duplicate settings entry. The download token is now its own setting: huggingfaceDownloadToken, stored as huggingface.downloadToken, env FUOBE_HF_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN. It is not HF_TOKEN, because main's llm-registry test forbids that variable. It sits in Settings → LoRAs as 'Hugging Face token for downloads', masked, with Save & test; the e2e confirmed the field is a password field.

Gated LoRAs: LoraRef.adapter is new. Optional gated LoRAs (Relight, DoP's Slow motion) are left out of cloud runs with the old note again, whether or not a token is set, and lorasFit counts them as before. Only fuobe-restore's own IC-LoRA (adapter: true) is sent to the cloud, as Fuobe's copy made with the token. createRestore refuses a paid cloud run with a 422 before anything starts when there is no token; placeholder runs don't need one.
mirrorCivitai builds its hosting note from the LoRA's hostedOk (gatedHosting), and the orphaned testCivitaiKey docblock is back in place.

Upscale → Video: the static `related` link became UPSCALE_FIRST_STEPS in src/lib/catalog/upscale-first.ts (StudioConfig.firstSteps, drawn by studio-page.tsx with a visible hint), so n7-3 can add its row there. 'Restore archive footage first' opens Restore & colourise with ?then=upscale. That turns on a new 'Then upscale' switch: planRestore's thenUpscale adds an upscale-video step after the sound is put back (SeedVR2 on the GPU, Topaz Video in the cloud, both to 2160p). The upscaled clip is the run's one result, and its price is included in the estimate. Restore to 4K and Then upscale can't both be on.

GPU pre-flight: a STUDIO_ROWS row for /video-tools/restore covering the restore graph, oss-join-clips, oss-mux and the gated Restore LoRA. ComfyUI-LTXVideo is pinned in workflows/comfyui/packs.json at 220e1d45 (registry id ComfyUI-LTXVideo, taken from its pyproject name; the registry API gave no answer). build-requirements.mjs now includes video-restore-ltx25-tiled in requirements.json.
Flaky test: batchOf in tests/restore-api.test.ts now orders by rowid.

Tests: new tests/restore-signup.test.ts (proxy answers for guests, accounts and the owner; visitor pricing; the 4 MB body; the board row). Also extended restore, restore-api, public-signup and lora-fetch, and adjusted gpu-requirements (gated set; budget raised from 25 to 26 KB gzipped, from 24.8 KB before this graph) and settings-links (now reads lora-settings.tsx anchors). The e2e script gained the Upscale-to-Restore chain checks.
impl.tests: tsc clean, and eslint clean on every changed file. Targeted vitest (--maxWorkers=2) after the second base merge: 35 files, 603 tests passed (restore*, public-signup*, lora-fetch, fal-lora, gpu-*, comfy-library-4, settings-*, llm-*, canvas*, eval-harness, request-body-limits and others). The full suite was not run. tests/e2e/restore-flows.mjs ran against a placeholder-mode dev server (FUOBE_DEMO_MODE=on; demo mode now defaults to off on main) and all checks passed, twice, the second time after the second merge. That covers the GPU and cloud flows, the placeholder run with its Before/After wipe, Upscale → Restore with Then upscale on, the masked token, Shorts and the Explainer offering the restore step, and 6 pages at 1440 and 390 px in light and dark on both engines with no sideways scroll. I also looked at the 390 px dark screenshot. ComfyUI: validate-workflows on the live CPU server still fails with missing_node_type for the ComfyUI-LTXVideo nodes (expected; I reverted its object_info and validation-state rewrites, which were only noise).
left: Faceless gets no old-footage upload. Faceless takes only scripts (text) and reference images, and generates every shot itself, so offering a restore step would mean a new clip-upload path in its episode plan. I left that out; Shorts and the Explainer have the step.

Deinterlace still drops one field (fieldHeight = height/2, nearest rows) instead of the card's fieldmatch,yadif,decimate. ComfyUI has no such nodes, and the Fuobe server runs no ffmpeg pre-pass for the open engine. The UI note says so.

Never run on a GPU: the graph is validated:false because the CPU ComfyUI lacks ComfyUI-LTXVideo. Tiled fusion, the 17-frame prefix hand-off, the reference at frame_idx -1 and Restore to 4K are unproven. GPU_NOTE ('24 GB class, minutes per window') is unmeasured.
Needs real keys: the cloud route (fal LTX-2.3 reference-video-to-video/lora with the mirrored gated LoRA), the token download (HF token plus accepted licence), and Then upscale on Topaz Video.
model-pins.json has no pins for the two gated LoRA files: their sha256 can't be read without a token. The library entries carry their sizes and pinned revisions.
Optional gated LoRAs no longer go to the cloud even when a token is set. That is a deliberate return to the pre-branch behaviour; extending it is a later choice.
Assist/MCP restore_video has no 'then upscale' argument.
Needs a GPU ComfyUI with ComfyUI-LTXVideo, a real fal key and a Hugging Face token with the gated licences accepted (not blocking).
docsNotes: docs/public-signup.md: add Restore & colourise to the own-gpu-tool list (POST /api/restore, /api/restore/prompt) and /api/restore/estimate to the price checks.

Settings docs: Settings → LoRAs has 'Hugging Face token for downloads' (FUOBE_HF_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN), separate from Assist's Hugging Face key (FUOBE_HF_TOKEN). It is only for gated LoRAs (Lightricks' Restore and Detail Refine IC-LoRAs), and a cloud run gets Fuobe's copy, never the token.

FEATURES / STATUS: Video tools → Restore & colourise (both engines; GPU tiled LTX-2.5 with Restore to 4K, deinterlace and reference; cloud LTX-2.3 untiled at 720p or 1080p). Upscale → Video's 'Restore archive footage first' runs restore then upscale in one job. Restore entries are in the Library and feed menus, a Canvas Restore node, the Shorts and Explainer old-footage offer, and Assist/MCP restore_video.

ARCHITECTURE: LoraRef.adapter (a model's own gated adapter, the only gated LoRA that goes to the cloud) and src/lib/catalog/upscale-first.ts (Upscale's list of first steps; n7-3 adds its Regenerate in 2K row there).

Where the brief was out of date: it says the token goes in 'Settings → Connections', but there is no such section; it lives in Settings → LoRAs. The brief's HF token env would have clashed with main's HF_TOKEN rule. The brief's assumption that this branch's acc-2 handler() exists in the base was already noted in the WIP. Demo mode now defaults to off, so the e2e needs FUOBE_DEMO_MODE=on.
scripts/comfy/README.md has the Restore section next to main's Round 5 section (both kept).

findings.title: The full Vitest suite fails: 3 tests in 2 files, all caused by this branch
findings.detail: Full run (FUOBE_ACCOUNT_DISK_FREE_GB=1, --maxWorkers=2): 285 files, 4541 tests, 3 failed, 4535 passed, 3 skipped. Both test files are the same as on base claude/fuobe-parity-4. (1) tests/comfy-library-notes.test.ts, 'video-restore-ltx25-tiled reads as a public note' and 'the spec's notes are as clean as the manifest's': the graph's notes end 'Not validated here: the pack is not installed on this server.' (scripts/comfy/library.spec.mjs:2823, copied into workflows/comfyui/manifest.json), and 'on this server' is one of the INTERNAL patterns the test bans. (2) tests/model-access-listings.test.ts:100 expects list.loras.length 174 and gets 176, because the branch adds two LoRAs (Restore and Detail Refine). The targeted list in the implementer's report left out both files. Running only these two files fails the same way every time.
findings.verified: Full suite run and a rerun of the two files; git diff of both test files against base is empty

findings.title: Cloud engine: the reference picture is silently dropped from the Restore pipeline
findings.detail: planRestore's cloud branch (src/lib/catalog/restore.ts, about lines 467-520) never reads input.reference. No piece gets inputs.images: piece 0 has no image at all, and later pieces get only the hand-off frame. The UI still offers it: the 'First frame in colour (optional)' slot and the hint 'The cloud uses a picture as the clip's first frame'. src/server/restore.ts planInput adds the estimate note 'In the cloud your picture is the first frame', and the Assist/MCP restore_video description says the same, so the user is told their picture is used when it isn't. The open branch does pass it (inputs.images on every window). Probe: planRestore({engine:'cloud', ..., reference:'/api/files/ref.png'}) gives steps cut0 / restore0 (and hand1 / restore1 / join) with no images on restore0. No test covers a cloud reference.
findings.verified: Probe test run against the branch's code (vitest with a scratch config; no edits to the worktree)

findings.title: routeLoras gives the wrong reason for optional gated LoRAs (regression from removing the gated line in plan.ts)
findings.detail: The branch removed `if (gated(l) && !l.hostedUrl) return "it is in a gated Hugging Face repo, so it runs only on your GPU"` from routeLoras' why() in src/lib/catalog/plan.ts. An optional gated LoRA left off a cloud route (Relight, DoP's Slow motion) now falls through to 'no URL to send to the LoRA endpoint'. previewGeneration returns that in loras.dropped, which the evaluation harness records. Probe: routeLoras(fuobe-restore's fal route, [ltx-2-5-22b-lora-slow-motion-control]) gives dropped reason 'no URL to send to the LoRA endpoint'. This contradicts the report's 'gated LoRAs behave as before'. fitLoras' user-facing note is unchanged and correct. A fix is to keep the line with `&& !l.adapter`.

findings.title: Requirement index: the gzip budget raise is justified, but the raw 200 KB budget is now 99.8% full
findings.detail: requirements.json on base: 202,120 B raw, 25,466 B gzipped (24.87 KB). On the branch: 204,422 B raw, 25,880 B gzipped (25.27 KB). This graph and its pack push gzip past the 25 KB limit, so raising it to 26 KB is a small, documented and warranted change. The raw limit (200*1024 = 204,800 B) was left alone and has only 378 B left, so the next graph (n7-3-regenerate-2k is queued against the same index) will fail it. Raise or rethink both limits together, deliberately. The gated-set regex change in the same test is correct: both IC-LoRA repos really are gated.
findings.verified: Measured with zlib on git show of both refs

findings.title: GPU pre-flight row checks a different join graph from the one the pipeline runs
findings.detail: The STUDIO_ROWS row for /video-tools/restore lists REMOVE_TOOLS.open.join = oss-join-clips (video-concat-{n}: BatchImagesNode/CreateVideo/ImageScale). planRestore joins windows with oss-join-encoded (video-concat-encoded: ConcatenateVideo). On a ComfyUI without ConcatenateVideo the board could say Ready while a multi-window run fails at the join. tests/restore-signup.test.ts only checks that the listed workflows exist.
findings.verified: Read src/server/gpu/tools.ts, src/lib/catalog/restore.ts joinEncoded and requirements.json

findings.title: Visitor estimates reveal the owner's token state and show an owner-only instruction
findings.detail: POST /api/restore/estimate is open to guests and accounts (ESTIMATES, priceAs). It returns hfToken: hasHfToken(), which says whether the install owner has set a Hugging Face download token. When none is set it adds GATED_NOTE ('add your Hugging Face token in Settings → LoRAs'), which a visitor can't do; Fuobe never downloads onto an account's GPU anyway. The token itself never leaves the server. This is a boolean leak plus a misleading note: give a visitor's estimate hfToken true (or leave it out) and drop the note under tenant().

findings.title: Cloud run refused without a token even when Fuobe already holds a copy; the setup panel nags on the GPU when the file is already there
findings.detail: createRestore throws 422 on any paid cloud run when !hasHfToken(). It doesn't check that prepareCloudLoras would use a cached fal copy (getCopy within the TTL) or a pinned local file (mirrorCivitai's sha-checked local lookup). An owner who mirrored once and then removed the token is blocked for no reason. On the open engine, the 'One-time setup: the Restore IC-LoRA is gated' panel shows whenever no token is set, even if the LoRA file is already in ComfyUI's loras folder.
findings.verified: Read src/server/restore.ts createRestore, src/server/loras.ts prepareCloudLoras/mirrorCivitai and restore-tool.tsx

findings.title: Mirroring the 1.7 GB LoRA holds the whole file in memory twice
findings.detail: mirrorCivitai reads the file with fs.readFileSync (1.71 GB), and fal's prepareFile wraps it in new Uint8Array(data), which copies it into the File. Peak memory is about 3.4 GB or more on the Next server. The pattern already existed for civitai LoRAs, but this is the first adapter this large. Not verified live: it needs real fal keys.

findings.title: Weak tests around the new paths
findings.detail: In lora-fetch's 'with the token' case, only the refusal on a hash mismatch is tested. The success path (copied once, recorded with the gatedHosting licence note, hostedUrl in the payload, the cache reused on the next run) and createRestore's 422 without a token on a real (non-placeholder) cloud plan aren't covered. No test checks the cloud reference (finding 2). The 3 suite failures show that the targeted test list missed affected files.

findings.title: Pins and sizes of the gated LoRAs
findings.detail: The report says model-pins.json has no pins because the sha256 can't be read without a token. But lora-library.generated.ts has both files' sha256 and exact sizes (1,711,643,914 and 1,308,787,534 B), while requirements.json carries rounded sizes (1.71e9 and 1.31e9).

checks: Full Vitest (FUOBE_ACCOUNT_DISK_FREE_GB=1, --maxWorkers=2): 285 files, 4541 tests; 3 failed (comfy-library-notes x2, model-access-listings x1), 4535 passed, 3 skipped. The failures are deterministic and caused by this branch.

tsc --noEmit: clean apart from the global LayoutProps/PageProps/RouteContext types that `next typegen` generates (no .next in the worktree); none in branch code. eslint on changed files: 0 errors, 1 warning that is already on base (WAN_NEG_EN).

huggingfaceDownloadToken: secret: true (masked by publicSettings). /api/settings, /api/providers/test and /api/loras writes are OWNER_WRITES; /api/loras GET is closed to guests. The token goes only as an Authorization header to the library entry's huggingface.co URL (taken from the library, not the request, so no SSRF). A local two-origin test on Node 22.23 confirmed that fetch drops Authorization on a cross-origin redirect. hfFacts uses redirect: manual; redact() masks the token; the copy record's sourceUrl has no token; fal receives only the mirrored hostedUrl. It is separate from huggingfaceToken and HF_TOKEN.

Gated LoRAs in the cloud: fitLoras still leaves out optional gated LoRAs (Relight, Slow motion) with the old note, with or without a token (lora-fetch test). Only the adapter: true Restore LoRA is sent, through the mirror. In tenant() it is refused rather than sent. Accounts' own-ComfyUI runs skip the download and go through checkAccountLoras with restoreGraphLoras.

settings-links test change is justified: restore-tool links /settings#huggingface; ConnectField id='huggingface' renders as the wrapper div's id in lora-settings.tsx, which the anchor set didn't read before; its labels sit under Settings → LoRAs.
gpu-requirements: the gated regex is correct (both IC-LoRA repos are gated). The gzip budget raise 25→26 KB is justified (24.87→25.27 KB), but the raw budget has 378 B left (finding 4).

Fetched fal's live OpenAPI for fal-ai/ltx-2.3-22b/reference-video-to-video/lora: video_url, image_url, negative_prompt, num_frames, fps, seed, video_size {width,height}, loras[{path,scale,weight_name}] (required), ic_lora_type none, preprocessor none, enable_prompt_expansion, generate_audio, match_video_length and match_input_fps all exist, so the generated FieldMap matches.

Checked the restore graph against the live CPU ComfyUI's /object_info: every core node's inputs match (the only misses are combo file lists and SaveVideo's dynamic format.codec). The three ComfyUI-LTXVideo nodes are missing there, as expected. Fetched the pinned pack (220e1d45) as data: the input names of LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide, LTXICLoRALoaderModelOnly and LTXVTiledFusionSampler match the graph, and the guide's tile_frames is 97, same as the sampler's when streaming. The pack's LICENSE is the LTX-2 Community License, matching licences.ts. Its network code (gemma_api_conditioning) is a node this graph doesn't use. Nothing installed and no restart.

Public sign-up: /api/restore and /api/restore/prompt aren't in accountMayChange, so guests and accounts get own-gpu-tool. /api/restore/estimate is in ESTIMATES and goes through priceAs. tests/public-signup and restore-signup pass.
No LoRA files, Higgsfield media or binaries committed; no Higgsfield API use. Licences are recorded for both IC-LoRAs (library), the cloud model, the manifest entry and the node pack.

Hand-built and workflows/ copies of the graph match apart from formatting, and validation-state's sha256 matches the workflow file. SeedVR2's chunked graph keeps audio, so Then upscale on the GPU keeps the restored sound.
Did not rerun the browser e2e at 1440 and 390 px (the implementer reports two passes). Did not touch /home/user/Fuobe.
review.verdict: changes requested: fix the 3 failing tests (reword the graph note without 'on this server' and update the LoRA count to 176), pass the cloud reference picture to piece 0 (or remove the cloud reference UI, note and Assist text), and restore the gated reason in routeLoras. The low findings can follow. The token handling and the gated-LoRA cloud behaviour are sound.

applied: Merged claude/fuobe-parity-4 at 2c72d369, which includes o/dbs-d2 (Remove dialogue), into o/archive-restore as merge commit e2641d36. One conflict, a docblock in src/components/studio/mode-switch-studio.tsx: kept both Remove dialogue and Restore & colourise. origin/claude/fuobe-parity-4 has since moved to that same 2c72d369, so the branch is up to date with it.

Finding 1 (3 failing tests): the video-restore-ltx25-tiled note no longer ends with 'Not validated here: the pack is not installed on this server' (changed in scripts/comfy/library.spec.mjs and workflows/comfyui/manifest.json together; the rebuilt requirements.json is byte-identical). tests/model-access-listings.test.ts now expects 176 LoRAs, with a comment naming the two IC-LoRAs.

Finding 2 (cloud reference): planRestore's cloud branch now sends input.reference as images[0] on piece 0, which fal sends as image_url. A single whole piece gets the video and the image. A cut piece gets the image, and the cut arrives through the chain. Later pieces still start from the hand-off frame. New test in tests/restore.test.ts covers the multi-piece case (including withChainInputs merging the chained cut beside the picture), the whole-clip case, and no reference. The existing fal payload test already checks that images[0] maps to image_url.

Finding 3 (routeLoras reason): the gated line is back in src/lib/catalog/plan.ts as `gated(l) && !l.hostedUrl && !l.adapter`. New test in tests/eval-api.test.ts: on the reference-video-to-video/lora route, DoP's Slow-motion LoRA is dropped with the gated reason and Restore's adapter is applied.

Finding 4 (requirement-index budget): raised, not shrunk. tests/gpu-requirements.test.ts now allows 216 KB raw and 27 KB gzipped, with a comment explaining why: this graph took the index from 202.1 to 204.4 KB (24.9 to 25.3 KB gzipped), and each graph adds about 1-2.5 KB raw and 0.2-0.5 KB gzipped, so the next few graphs, n7-3's among them, now fit. I raised both limits together, as the review advised, because 26 KB gzipped had only 0.7 KB left. The index is already compact JSON, so shrinking it would mean a format change for its readers.

Finding 5 (pre-flight join): the STUDIO_ROWS row for /video-tools/restore now lists RESTORE_OPEN_JOIN (oss-join-encoded, newly exported from src/lib/catalog/restore.ts and used by joinEncoded) instead of oss-join-clips. tests/restore-signup.test.ts builds a multi-window GPU plan with sound and checks that the row's workflows are exactly the ones that plan uses, including video-concat-encoded.

Finding 6 (visitor estimate): under tenant() (a guest or an account priced through priceAs), the estimate leaves out the token-state field and does not add GATED_NOTE. The field is renamed from hfToken to an optional loraReady (src/server/restore.ts, src/components/restore/hooks.ts). The setup panel shows only when loraReady === false. New test: neither a guest nor an account sees loraReady or the gated or Settings → LoRAs note; the owner with no token sees loraReady false and the note.

Finding 7 (cloud refusal and GPU nag): new gatedFileReady(file, target) in src/server/loras.ts. It counts as ready when there is a token, or a live copy on the provider within its TTL (cloud only), or the file in ComfyUI's LoRA folder (and, for the cloud, Fuobe's cache) at its pinned size. Size stands in for the hash so an estimate doesn't hash 1.7 GB; mirrorCivitai still checks the hash before sending. createRestore now refuses a paid cloud run with 422 only when no usable copy exists. On the GPU, the estimate's loraReady and the setup panel check the folder, and with Restore to 4K on they check the Detail Refine file too.

Finding 9 (missing tests): tests/lora-fetch.test.ts has a new success path, using the Detail Refine IC-LoRA pinned to a small stand-in as an adapter. With the token it is downloaded once (the token is never in a URL), copied to fal, and recorded with its sha256, size, sourceUrl and the gatedHosting note 'its licence allows hosted use'. A second run without the token reuses the copy with no network call. gatedFileReady is checked for fal and replicate, with and without the cache. tests/restore-api.test.ts has a new readiness test: with no token, a live fal copy lets the run through the 422 guard (it is stopped at a mocked createPipeline, so nothing is submitted), an expired copy is not ready, and a file in the LoRA folder at its pinned size is ready on both engines (a sparse file, so nothing is written). Restore to 4K without the refine file is not ready, and a file of the wrong size is not. The existing 422 test without a token on a real (fal key, non-placeholder) cloud plan now also checks that the estimate says loraReady false.

fix.finalSummary: o/archive-restore at 3f54b012, merged with claude/fuobe-parity-4 2c72d369 (Remove dialogue included). Open engine (ComfyUI): Restore & colourise runs the tiled-fusion LTX-2.5 graph with the Restore IC-LoRA, 97-frame windows chained by a 17-frame prefix, the optional reference at frame_idx -1, a one-field deinterlace, the sound put back, an optional Restore to 4K detail pass and an optional Then upscale (SeedVR2). The setup panel and the gated note now show only while neither a Hugging Face token nor the LoRA file in ComfyUI's folder is there. The pre-flight row checks the packet-copy join the pipeline really runs. All of this is built and unit-tested, but it has never run on a GPU: the graph is validated:false because the CPU ComfyUI lacks ComfyUI-LTXVideo. Cloud engine (fal LTX-2.3 reference-video-to-video/lora): untiled pieces of up to 97 frames at 720p or 1080p, each later piece starting from the last restored frame. The reference picture now really becomes the first piece's first frame (image_url), as the UI, the note and Assist say. The Restore LoRA goes as Fuobe's copy. A run without a token is refused only when Fuobe has no copy to send. Optional gated LoRAs stay off cloud routes with the gated reason. The plan and payload are tested, but nothing has run live: that needs a real fal key and a Hugging Face token with the licence accepted. Public sign-up: guests and accounts get own-gpu-tool on /api/restore and /api/restore/prompt. /api/restore/estimate prices them for their own GPU, never as a demo, and now tells them nothing about the owner's token or copies. The owner's flows are unchanged. Full suite, typecheck and lint pass.

Nit (pins and sizes): model-pins.json has no entries for the two gated files, though lora-library.generated.ts has their sha256 and exact sizes, and requirements.json shows rounded sizes. Adding pins from the library's values is a small follow-up.
The readiness check on the GPU reads the local LoRA folder (comfyLorasDir). A remote ComfyUI with no folder set still shows the setup panel until a token is added, which is harmless.

From the earlier stages, still open: Faceless has no old-footage upload. Deinterlace drops one field rather than running fieldmatch, yadif and decimate. The graph has never run on a GPU and GPU_NOTE's timing is unmeasured. The cloud route, the token download and Topaz Then upscale have never run with real keys. Assist/MCP restore_video has no 'then upscale' argument.
Docs notes from the implement report still apply: Restore in the public-signup own-gpu-tool and price lists, and the separate download-token setting.
